everyone aged 15 to 64 and it falls to 34th, below the Netherlands. Iceland goes the other way.

g.text: Rank of 40 OECD countries by annual hours worked, 2024
Left: the usual ranking. Right: the same hours spread over everyone of working age. Red fell 10+ places, blue rose 10+.

text.style: font-weight: 500; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-anchor: start; fill: #e4572e
font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17171a

g.text: Why: long hours, but fewer people working
Each country by employment rate and hours per worker. Dotted curves join equal hours per adult.
DATA OECD annual hours actually worked per worker; OECD employment rate, ages 15-64. 2024.
NOTE Hours per adult = hours per worker x employment rate. Hours cover workers of all ages.
Spearman correlation between the two rankings: 0.76.
